note: The roster of reference plates the sky's photographic pieces are ingested from. Everything in here is a number the pixels cannot answer for themselves: how much sky a frame spans, where the light was, how many bodies the frame is supposed to hold. The chain reads it, states what it made of each plate, and says so when a plate disagrees with its entry. Files are looked up by `file` first and by `id` second, so renaming a source is a one-line change.

notes.shoulderFromColour: whether this plate's coverage is rebuilt out of its own colour. Say it only for a source that is a cloud drawn OVER BLACK with a HARD MATTE laid on top of it, and check it against the line the run prints: 'light outside the matte', how many of the texels the matte calls empty still carry colour. On the fifteen of the alpha roster that is 27 to 74 per cent of them, at a mean of 0.06 to 0.22 in linear light — a shoulder the matte is already nought across, which the chain was multiplying by that nought and throwing away. See reconstructShoulder in tools/clouds/ingest/lib/matte.mjs.
notes.veilKnee: the coverage under which the rebuilt shoulder is taken to nothing, softly, by the same curve the matting branch uses. It is a step in the DELIVERED frame and not a threshold on the plate: this material stands fifty to ninety display levels off its own sky, so twenty parts in 255 is where the shoulder's own step is under a tenth of a level and nothing can find it. Measured: between three and forty eight parts in 255 it moves the plate's veil share by a point and a half, because the tail it cuts is already thinner than the knee.
notes.veilGamma: how much of the rebuilt shoulder is taken, as a power on it. THIS IS A DECLARED CHOICE AND NOT A MEASUREMENT, and the reason is that one observation cannot carry two answers: a texel of premultiplied plate is a times C, and the light standing round a silhouette is partly cloud that occludes and partly cloud that scatters forward past it, which no division can separate. At one the hero's own veil share is 31.8 per cent and its shoulder still carries a fortieth of coverage five degrees out, which reaches the margin of the plate on three sides and takes the body with it; at two it is 28.0, against the reference's 28.5 for a whole frame, and the margins come back under the ceiling. It is fitted on the DELIVERED frame's thickness histogram against the reference's, which is the only place the question is asked.
notes.density: how many times its own depth a piece is drawn at. A matte carries the coverage the PHOTOGRAPH had — this bank, at this distance, through that day's air — and what the world wants is a deck that closes. Coverage is one minus an exponential of the depth, so d times the depth is 1-(1-a)^d: nought stays nought, one stays one, and only the veil in between thickens. It is not a threshold and it cuts nothing; it is the one knob that answers 'the cloud reads translucent' at the cause instead of at the silhouette.
notes.spanDeg: horizontal angle the whole plate covers. It sets every piece's angular size and therefore how large the sky draws it; there is no way to read it off the pixels, and it is the first thing to check against the source. Where a source's own lens is not recorded — which is all nine of these — the value stated is the one at which the plate's cloud delivers, at unit scale, the angular size the reference measures for the part it is to play: the hero's 51 degrees against the reference's principal mass of 53.2, the deck's 68 against the band under eight degrees. Composing with a scale far from one instead would say the same thing in a place where nothing records it.
notes.sunElevation: height of the sun in the plate, in degrees. The roster of sources is shot backlit at thirty to thirty five, and this is set to the WORLD's own sun inside that range: a piece then standing at its own height and at the world sun's bearing plus its own offset is lit by exactly the light it was photographed under, and the runtime's relighting ratio is one. Every other placement is a departure from that pose and is relit by however far it departs.
notes.sunAzimuthOffset: bearing of the sun relative to the middle of the plate. Nought means straight behind the mass.
notes.degree: order of the surface the background is estimated as. Two is a gradient with a broad brightening in it. Three follows a stronger halo and is likelier to follow a cloud as well: raise it only when the residual asks.
notes.floor: how many multiples of the plate's own coverage noise the soft knee sits at. It is a knee and not a threshold — see tools/clouds/ingest/lib/matte.mjs — and zero disables it.
notes.dilateDeg: how far apart two lobes may be and still be one body. Generous welds bodies the source separated on purpose.
notes.minSolidDeg: the smallest window a body is worth cutting.
notes.minBodyDeg: how much cloud a body has to be, as the side of the square of solid coverage it is worth. It is what tells a wisp from a speck of grain, and it is an amount rather than a size.
notes.reachDeg: how far past its own body a window may be pushed looking for quiet. Every texel of a frame belongs to some body, so without a bound two bodies each take the whole plate.
notes.edgeCeiling: the most coverage an edge of a window may carry, averaged along it, before the body is called cut by the frame and discarded. Read as a step in the delivered frame: this material stands about fifty display levels off its own sky, so a tenth of coverage is five levels and that is where a wisp stops being a wisp.
notes.fadeDeg: how wide the band is that brings an edge under the ceiling to nothing. Degrees, so the slope it draws is a fraction of a level across a whole degree of sky. What it removes is measured and written into the manifest.
notes.texelDeg: degrees of sky one texel of the atlas spans for THIS plate, when a coarser rate than the atlas's own is right for it. A cumulus has a silhouette a tenth of a degree across; a sheet of high cirrus has no silhouette at all and is drawn thirty degrees wide, so a texel twice the size is a texel nobody can find. The coarser of the two wins: a plate cannot ask to be sharper than the atlas has decided to be.
notes.bodies: how many pieces this plate is expected to yield. The chain does not enforce it; it says so when what it found differs, which is what catches a dilation set wrong.
notes.featherDeg: how far a border runs, in degrees of THE SKY AS DRAWN and not of the plate — the one width in this roster that is not the plate own, because it describes the picture and not the material. Taken in a plate own degrees it comes out as wide as a small piece whole window and hands the frame a rectangle of haze cut at that window margin. See the note over the border in tools/clouds/ingest/pack.mjs. Nought is exactly the behaviour before this line existed.
notes.featherMix: how much of the border is taken, nought to one. The operator is a PARTIAL blur of the premultiplied pair, a + w(G(a)-a), so at one the rim is the piece seen through an aperture featherDeg wide and at nought it is the piece. Its mean coverage is the mean coverage and its half coverage contour does not move, which is why a composition stated in widths arrives at the size it asks for.
notes.featherHold: how far INSIDE the half coverage contour the stretching reaches, in multiples of featherDeg. This is the number that decides whether it is a border or a soft atlas: held two deep the band contrasts fall from 0.46 to 0.33 at ten degrees, the micro contrast from 2.94 to 1.77 and the largest mass from 78 per cent of the sky to 34, because half of a body six degrees across is within two of its own rim. Measured at six tenths the interior keeps what the source gave it.
notes.featherOut: how far OUTSIDE that contour it is allowed to go, in the same multiples. A Gaussian has no end — the kernel reaches three widths and a bank still writes a hundredth of coverage there, which is over CELL_LIVE, so the union of live cells swells to the frame of the window and the window cuts it: a rectangle of haze round every placement, shot and confirmed. At two the border ends before anything can cut it.
notes.featherShrinkDeg: how much the material is eroded before it is blurred, in degrees of the sky as drawn. It exists because a frame that calls a pixel cloud by a threshold cannot tell a soft edge from a bigger one, and it is delivered at NOUGHT: measured on this composition, a shrink of a sixth of a degree pays back a point of coverage and breaks the mass — the largest connected body falls from 58.5 per cent of the sky to 30 — because the five pieces of it overlap on thin material. The knob stays because the next composition may not be built that way; this one is.
notes.grainGain: what the material own modulation is raised to before it is stored, so that what comes out of the WORLD tone curve is the contrast the cloud actually has. One is exactly the behaviour before this line existed. Measured on the shipped chain, stage by stage (the stage-by-stage probe): the hero tile carries 67.4 per cent of inner span, the sampler hands it to the fragment whole at 68.8, compositing over the sky takes 7.9 points and the halo 1.3, and AgX takes THIRTY SIX AND A HALF - it compresses a ratio at this body luminance by a power of about 0.38, the same factor on the span and on the micro contrast. AgX is the world own curve and is not this chain to touch, so the material is written against it here. Two and two tenths is the frontier: at two and six tenths the coverage goes to 24.7 against a net of 24, the transition profile breaks, and the frame micro contrast FALLS - the material is being pushed into the shoulder harder than the expansion buys back.
notes.grainReachDeg: the scale above which the material is left alone, in degrees of THE SKY AS DRAWN and not of the plate - the same convention featherDeg uses and for the same reason. Everything wider than this is subtracted out, the rest raised to grainGain, and the wide part put back untouched: so a bank own top-to-bottom shading, the band contrasts, the mass and the silhouette see nothing, and only the modulation at the scale the eye reads as cauliflower is expanded. Taken globally instead, a twenty degree bank base goes dark enough to fall out of what metro14 calls cloud at all and the coverage net goes with it. Two and six tenths is metro14 own kernel with room round it; measured, five degrees buys nine tenths of a point of span over it and the knob saturates.

world.note: Where the world's own light is, copied into the manifest so the runtime can see at a glance that the atlas and the dome are lit by one sun. It is src/core/sky.js that owns the number at runtime.
world.aerialBakedNote: how much of THIS world's aerial perspective the plates already carry, nought to one. The renderer applies the term to every kind of weather it draws and multiplies it by one minus this, so one means the plates owe nothing and the frame is what it was before the number existed. It cannot be read off a plate — the matte closes a body's core by topology, so what a core falls short of one by says nothing about the air in front of it — and it is therefore fitted, like the four constants of the term itself, against the reference's own rise of contrast with height. that sweep carries the sweep.
world.plateSkyNote: the background a plate delivered WITH its own alpha was shot against, in that plate's own linear units. A matted source has no sky left in it, and the sky is the one number tools/clouds/ingest/pack.mjs calibrates a plate's level by, so it has to be stated or the chain stops. DERIVED FROM THIS DOME, not guessed: a plate is display referred, so the sky it would carry is this world's own dome as this world's own composite writes it — src/core/post.js, mirrored in the offline copy of it — read back through the sRGB transfer into the linear values a plate's pixels decode to. that derivation is the derivation and it takes one argument, the height the dome is read at, because the dome is three times the radiance at two degrees that it is at fifteen. Five degrees: the height a bank stands at in a photograph taken from the ground, and the only number in this line the pixels cannot check — it is where a plate's unrecorded exposure ends up. Set once for all fifteen, judged on whether the delivered frame's band contrasts land on the reference's, never touched per plate. What differs between one plate and another is `shoulder`, which is measured. REDERIVED AT DEV-C33, when the dome was refitted onto the target own blue: the same derivation at the same five degrees, run against the new preset, moves it from 0.13964/0.29022/0.40663 to 0.11182/0.26118/0.45197 — the dome at five degrees goes from display 105/146/170 to 94/140/179, which is the whole of what a bluer sky does to the sky a plate is calibrated against. that derivation is still the derivation and it was not touched.
world.cloudLevelNote: one gain per channel over every plate, and the only knob in this chain that is not a measurement of the plate. A photograph's highlights are compressed by a curve nobody recorded, so the cloud-to-sky ratio it carries is a floor, and the colour it carries is the colour of that exposure rather than of this world's light. THE CHROMATICITY IS FITTED, family by family, and the fit is the colour ruler: the delivered frame is cut into crown, body, belly and fringe over five bands from six degrees to twenty two, twenty pairs against the reference at the same elevation, and weighted over every family and band they agree on r/g to x1.0040 and on b/g to x1.0025. THE LUMINANCE IS A MEASUREMENT WITH A CEILING ON IT, AND THE CEILING IS THE COVERAGE NET, NOT THE COMPOSITE CURVE. The three channels are multiplied ALIKE, by 1.98 over what DEV-C8 shipped, and 1.98 is not a taste: it is the LOWEST gain that carries both of the things two gates asked for at once — the cloud's ninety ninth percentile on the reviewer's own rectangle (900,40 772x300) over 212, and the border step over 75 display levels. SWEPT AT THE RUNTIME ON THE DELIVERED COMPOSITION, one frame, f.hub.setCloudLevel, reported as gain / coverage per cent / p99 / border step L / median gap deg: x1.8 22.7 209.6 72.4 0.96 | x1.9 23.2 211.5 74.7 1.22 | x1.98 23.5 212.6 76.0 1.25 | x2.1 23.9 214.5 77.7 1.37 | x2.2 24.2 215.7 78.8 1.31 | x3.0 26.1 224.4 86.8 2.18. Above x2.1 the frame leaves 20 to 24 per cent, because the gain lifts the shoulder of every body over the instrument's own cloud threshold and the sky reads wider — so what binds this number is the coverage net and the median gap that rides with it, and the two are stated here rather than argued. The reference's p99 of 237.9 is a radiance of about eight on this composite's curve, five times what the material carries, and no gain reaches it before everything under it is white. Nothing clips at 1.98: the frame's 99.9th percentile stands at 215.5 of 255 and no cloud pixel touches 255 on any channel. RESWEPT AT DEV-C34, ON THE DOME DEV-C33 FITTED, and the two gates no longer both bind: x1.98 was the lowest gain that carried a border step over 75 AND a p99 over 212, and the step is a DIFFERENCE whose subtrahend moved. The plateau outside the silhouette went from 112.3 display levels on the old dome to 128.0 on this one, and the reference's own is 125.8 — so the old sky sat thirteen and a half levels under the reference and the new one sits two above it. Read on the quantity the gain actually moves, the plateau INSIDE, "step over 75" meant "inside over 187.3", and this delivery stands at 194.7. The p99 gate is untouched and reads 217.9 over 212. The sweep, one frame, f.hub.setCloudLevel, reported as gain / coverage per cent / cloud p50 / p99 on the reviewer's rectangle / border step L / inside plateau L / rms of the five band contrasts against the reference: x0.55 41.9 188.5 206.8 60.6 188.8 0.1068 | x0.65 44.3 193.7 212.1 65.1 193.1 0.0750 | x0.80 46.5 200.2 217.9 66.7 194.7 0.0630 | x0.90 47.6 203.7 221.1 68.9 197.1 0.0681 | x1.00 48.4 206.8 223.7 71.2 199.5 0.0795 | x1.15 49.0 210.9 227.2 74.8 203.3 0.0969 | x1.25 49.3 213.3 228.9 78.0 206.8 0.1088. The gain is x1.584 over what DEV-C8 shipped, which is x0.80 of x1.98, and three measurements that do not talk to each other choose it: the band contrast error has its minimum there, the cloud's own median lands on the reference's (200.2 against 201.1), and what is left of the distribution is SYMMETRIC — the tenth of a per cent stands 9.7 levels over the reference's and the ninety ninth 9.6 under it, which is a want of AMPLITUDE and not of level, and amplitude is the foot's to give. Nothing clips: the 99.9th stands at 224.0 of 255 and no cloud pixel touches 255 on any channel. that sweep carries the sweep.

plates.id: banco-a AND IT HAS BEEN MULTIPLIED BY 1.15 ON ALL THREE CHANNELS ALIKE, which moves the luminance and cannot move the chromaticity by a part in a thousand. Two things asked for it and both are measurements. The first is that the ingest no longer draws a straight colour as if it were premultiplied, so the frame writes the light the material actually has: over the whole atlas that was x1.18 of light removed, and the band contrasts fell with it. The second is that the reference still asks for more even after it — the colour ruler on the delivered frame reads r/g x1.0069, b/g x0.9919 and LUMINANCE x1.2082 weighted over every family and band, and metro14's own band contrasts read 0.23 against 0.31 at six degrees and 0.36 against 0.58 at twenty two. What a cloud must match is the distance it stands over the sky it is in front of, and that distance was short.

the default dilation welds two of its three: this plate keeps its lobes joined by a veil a third of the frame deep, and 0.06 of a degree is where the three the source separated come apart again.

the fragments, cast as the wisps of this composition. Their depth was tried at two thirds to raise the frame's veil share and it moved it by four tenths of a point, which is the measurement that says what density is: a MONOTONE map of the coverage, applied to every texel of a plate alike. metro14 reads thickness against the ninety ninth percentile of the cloud in the same band, so a map that moves the numerator and the denominator together cannot move the share at all. Only the SHAPE of a plate's own coverage can, and that is the source's.
cast as wisps, like alpha-08: see its note.

high veil, at the source's own coverage. Its depth was 0.65 and then 0.4 because the frame read it as a pale slab, and the slab was not the depth: the ingest was handing pack.mjs a STRAIGHT colour that the renderer then blended premultiplied, so this plate drew x3.81 the light its own material has and a fifth of its texels came out as neutral grey at the coverage. With that fixed there is nothing left for a depth under one to correct, and a source that brings its own matte has already answered the question depth is asked. skyBalance is 1 for the same reason it is not a half any more: see the note over tintAt in tools/clouds/ingest/pack.mjs.

the cumulus overhead, and the one plate above thirty degrees that is a BODY and not a veil. Its depth was 0.9 and is now one, which is what every plate of this set is: with the premultiply put right there is nothing for a depth under one to correct, and a source that brings its own matte has already answered the question. It carries no skyBalance, because a body's light is its own and not the sky's.
front lit, for the quadrant opposite the sun. Never mirrored and never relit: the light in these pixels is painted facing the eye and no ratio of two shadings of a matte can turn it round.

QUELLA LASTRA PORTAVA L'ARCO che il gate 17 boccia alla voce 1 (crop A1b: mezzo disco liscio con interno lattiginoso). Le tre strade che il gate lasciava aperte sono state provate tutte e tre con i numeri. (b) la torre presa dentro un banco: cade con la stessa misura, perche' la catena ritaglia attorno al CORPO e non attorno al quadro, quindi stringere la camera sposta i texel e non la sagoma. Le silhouette dei dieci volumi interi sono misurate tutte (lo scandaglio del campo) e cloud_01 a rotazione 0 e' la piu' alta, largo/alto 1,433, contro 1,621 di cloud_08 — che DEV-C22 aveva provato e che alla campata vera legge 1,748 — e 1,627 di cloud_09. cloud_05 INTERA di faccia (rot 0). RESA DAL VOLUME INTERO, SENZA NESSUN TAGLIO. Nella stesura di DEV-C21 questa lastra era ritagliata con un ellissoide, e dove un ellissoide morde materia densa lascia un ARCO DI CERCHIO: contro il blu un arco si legge come fabbricato esattamente come un piano, solo curvo (la carta e' la carta della lastra). Allargare la sfumatura non lo cura — provato a 0,10 / 0,24 / 0,38 e messo a foglio, l'arco si sfoca e RESTA un arco. Un volume intero non ha nessun bordo fabbricato: il suo contorno e' tutto e solo quello che il simulatore ha scritto. Quali lastre lo portassero non e' stato ricordato ma MISURATO, da il misuratore d'arco, che porta il cuore di tagli42 sull'alpha della lastra ricampionata ai 37,2 px per grado del quadro — la scala e' obbligatoria, perche RETTA conta punti con una tolleranza in pixel e le lastre stanno fra 15 e 154 px per grado.
